text: Shubhneet Singh, born on 10 August 1997, is an Indian rapper-singer and songwriter based in Canada, known professionally as Shubh, and associated with Punjabi music. He rose to mainstream popularity in 2021 with the single "We Rollin" and released his debut album, Still Rollin, in 2023. His singles, including "Elevated," "Offshore," "No Love," "Baller," and "Her," have charted on the Canadian Hot 100, New Zealand Chart, UK Singles Chart, and Billboard India. "Baller," produced by Ikky, became his most streamed track and reached number 68 on the Canadian Hot 100. The album Still Rollin debuted at number 16 on the Billboard Canadian Albums Chart and charted on the New Zealand Albums Chart; "Cheques" from the album peaked at number 3 on Billboard India Songs. Shubh was born in Punjab, India, to a Punjabi Sikh family and has an elder brother, Ravneet Singh, who is an actor, singer, vocalist, and host. He began his musical career in Brampton, Canada. In August 2023, he announced the Still Rolling world tour across seven countries—India, UK, Australia, New Zealand, UAE, USA, and Canada—divided into seven phases. The India phase included 10 cities and a cruise event at Cruise Control 4.0 in Mumbai aboard the Cordelia Cruise, but on 20 September 2023, BookMyShow announced the cancellation of the India tour, following the withdrawal of sponsorship by electronics brand boAt due to controversy. The UK phase featured concerts in London and Birmingham. On 5 January 2024, Shubh released his first EP, Leo, under his own label. On 29 March 2024, he released the single "Bandana" without prior announcement. On 10 April 2024, he announced the Aus/Nz phase, including concerts in Melbourne, Brisbane, Auckland, and Sydney, with tickets available on Shubhtour.com starting 3 May 2024; the Brisbane show on 4 May was cancelled due to promoter mismanagement and lack of communication, resulting in the revocation of the show permit due to venue load issues. On 3 May in Melbourne, Shubh performed his unreleased song "MVP," which was later released on his YouTube channel on 10 May 2024. In March 2023, during a curfew in Punjab due to a police search for pro-Khalistan separatist Amritpal Singh and internet shutdowns, Shubh shared an Instagram story titled "Pray for Punjab," featuring a distorted map created by Amandeep Singh (pseudonym Inkquisitive), showing Punjab, Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh darkened and omitting northeastern states and Jammu and Kashmir, which drew criticism for misrepresenting India. Actress Kangana Ranaut accused the post of indirect support for the Khalistan movement. Shubh removed the story and replaced it with "Pray for Punjab" on a black background. Inkquisitive later apologised, stating it was not intended to provoke a separate state agenda but to depict a "blackout in Punjab." On 19 September 2023, Inkquisitive reiterated the intent and blamed Ranaut for giving it a "pro-khalistan angle." On 21 September, Shubh clarified his concern over the internet shutdown in Punjab and expressed disappointment over the tour cancellation, stating, "India is my country too." Artists such as AP Dhillon, Karan Aujla, and Sidhu Moose Wala's team, along with politicians including Harsimrat Kaur Badal, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, and Bikram Singh Majithia, publicly supported him. During a London concert on 29 October 2023, Shubh held up a black hoodie thrown by the audience, allegedly bearing the date and image of the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by her bodyguards Satwant Singh and Beant Singh on a map of Punjab; he later posted that many items, including clothing, jewellery, and phones, were thrown at him, which he did not inspect, along with a video.
